d_sv_content.name: Advancing Non-Invasive Care for Dogs with Lymphoma
d_sv_content.tagline: Exploring a non-invasive, non-chemotherapy option to target lymphoma tumors.
d_sv_content.description:
Canine lymphoma is a common cancer in dogs that often affects lymph nodes. While chemotherapy remains an established treatment, researchers are exploring additional approaches.


This study is evaluating the safety and feasibility of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU), a non-invasive technology that uses focused sound waves to destroy targeted tumor tissue for canine lymphoma. Beyond killing a portion of the tumor cells in the lymph node, this treatment may help stimulate the immune system to recognize cancer cells.
d_sv_content.requirements: Participation involves approximately 3–4 hospital visits over a 30-day period. Dogs enrolled in the study will receive veterinary examinations, laboratory testing, and medical imaging.On the treatment day, HIFU will be used to treat a targeted lymph node. Sedation and/or general anesthesia will be required for the procedure.Beginning 8 days after the HIFU procedure, the dog will receive doxorubicin chemotherapy. The study covers the cost of five doxorubicin chemotherapy treatments, an established treatment option for canine lymphoma.
d_sv_content.whoCan: We are looking for dogs that have: Confirmed diagnosis of nodal B or T cell lymphoma Targeted lymph node is prescapular (in front of the shoulder blade) or popliteal (behind the knee)
d_sv_content.benefits: Participation may help researchers learn more about the potential use of focused ultrasound for canine lymphoma and could contribute to improved treatment options for pets in the future.Possible side effects from the HIFU treatment are generally expected to be mild to moderate and may include tiredness, soreness near the treated area, and swelling. Some dogs may also experience skin irritation, mild burns, or small sores or scabs over the treated area.
d_sv_content.compensation: All study-related costs are covered by the study sponsor, including medical imaging, bloodwork, HIFU treatment, and five doxorubicin chemotherapy treatments.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: A month period with 3-4 hospital visits.
